Calculate Neighbourhood Somatic Hypermutation Statistics

Source: R/nhood_shm.R
nhood_shm.Rd

Computes per-neighbourhood somatic hypermutation (SHM) summary statistics from B cell receptor (BCR) data stored in colData. For each neighbourhood, the function aggregates SHM metrics across cells that carry BCR information, and flags neighbourhoods with insufficient BCR coverage as unreliable.

Usage

nhood_shm(
  object,
  nhood_col = NULL,
  shm_cols = c("mu_count_VDJ", "mu_count_VJ", "mu_freq_VDJ", "mu_freq_VJ", "mu_count",
    "mu_freq"),
  min_n_shm = 20,
  summary_metric = "mean",
  result_name = "nhood_shm"
)

Arguments

object

A Milo or SingleCellExperiment object. Seurat objects must first be converted via as.SingleCellExperiment.

nhood_col

Character string. For plain SingleCellExperiment objects (i.e. not Milo), the name of the colData column containing neighbourhood assignments. Not required for Milo objects.

shm_cols

Character vector of column names in colData(object) containing per-cell SHM metrics to aggregate. Defaults to c("mu_count_VDJ", "mu_count_VJ", "mu_freq_VDJ", "mu_freq_VJ", "mu_count", "mu_freq"). All specified columns must be present in colData; missing columns will raise an error.

min_n_shm

Integer. Minimum number of cells with SHM annotation required for a neighbourhood's SHM statistics to be considered reliable. Neighbourhoods with fewer than min_n_shm contigs are retained in the output but have shm_reliable = FALSE and NA values for all SHM columns. Default is 10.

summary_metric

Character string specifying the central tendency statistic to compute for each SHM metric within each neighbourhood. One of "mean" (default) or "median". The corresponding spread metric is computed automatically: standard deviation (sd) for "mean", interquartile range (IQR) for "median".

result_name

Character string. Name of the metadata slot in which to store the resulting SHM data frame, i.e. the results are accessible via metadata(object)[[result_name]]. If the slot already exists it will be overwritten with a warning. Default is "nhood_shm".

Value

The input object with an additional (or updated) entry in metadata(object)[[result_name]]. The stored value is a data.frame with one row per neighbourhood and the following columns:

nhood

Neighbourhood identifier.

nhood_size

Total number of cells in the neighbourhood.

n_shm

Number of cells with at least one non-NA SHM value.

shm_capture_rate

Proportion of neighbourhood cells with SHM data (n_shm / nhood_size).

shm_reliable

Logical; TRUE if n_shm >= min_n_shm.

<shm_col>_<summary_metric>

One column per entry in shm_cols containing the aggregated statistic (mean or median).

<shm_col>_<spread_metric>

One column per entry in shm_cols containing the spread statistic (sd or IQR).

The data frame also carries the following attributes: min_n_shm, shm_cols, summary_metric, and spread_metric.

Details

Object type handling

  • Milo objects: Neighbourhood membership is read directly from the sparse nhoods matrix via nhoods. Row names of this matrix must match colnames(object); a mismatch raises an error to prevent silent misassignment.

  • Plain SingleCellExperiment objects: A binary neighbourhood membership matrix is constructed internally from the column specified by nhood_col. Cells with NA assignments are excluded with a warning.

SHM reliability flag

The shm_reliable flag is intended to help downstream filtering. Neighbourhoods below min_n_shm will have NA for all SHM statistics and should generally be excluded from differential SHM analyses.

See also

nhood_diversity, nhood_annotation, nhood_annotation_props, nhood_cdr3_convergence

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# --- Milo object ---
milo_obj <- nhood_shm(
  object = milo_obj,
  shm_cols = c("mu_freq_VDJ", "mu_freq_VJ", "mu_freq"),
  min_n_shm = 15,
  summary_metric = "median",
  result_name = "nhood_shm"
)

# Retrieve results
shm_df <- metadata(milo_obj)[["nhood_shm"]]
head(shm_df)

# --- Plain SingleCellExperiment object ---
sce_obj <- nhood_shm(
  object = sce_obj,
  nhood_col = "neighbourhood_id",
  min_n_shm = 10,
  summary_metric = "mean"
)
} # }
